subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should the remaining work stay in this combined macOS Gateway reliability issue, or be split into separate memory-backend soak and cron-alert resilience trackers?
rationale: The code now has partial fixes in multiple areas, but the remaining failure mode crosses memory watcher policy, QMD backend behavior, and whether cron alerts need a path independent from a wedged Gateway process.

options.title: Keep As Combined Reliability Tracker
options.body: Use this issue for maintainer-led macOS launchd soak validation and only close it when both memory growth and failure visibility are proven together.

options.title: Split Remaining Work
options.body: Create separate canonical items for QMD/memory soak proof and out-of-process or restart-aware cron alerting, then close this only after those canonical links own the leftovers.

options.title: Close After Release Retest
options.body: Ask reporters to retest v2026.6.11/current main and close only if the same workload no longer grows or silently drops cron failures.

recommendation.title: Keep As Combined Reliability Tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue for maintainer-led macOS launchd soak validation and only close it when both memory growth and failure visibility are proven together.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved user-visible gap is now centered on cron interrupted-run and failure-alert semantics after memory fixes landed.
